speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Bring Uncle a bar of soap, there's a good lad. Don't ask what it's for. It's for a mould. Of a key. Which I never mentioned.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Lovely. Smells of roses and conspiracy. You did well.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Pop this on the Crows' landing over on B wing. Put it down and walk away whistling. Don't open it. I mean it. I can see you thinking about it.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Ha! Kingy's face. Like a slapped haddock. Here's a drink for your trouble.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: {target} of the Crows told the whole canteen my mum's trifle was shop-bought. Have a quiet word. Loudly. With your fists.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: He'll think twice before slandering a homemade trifle. Have this, I've got loads.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Need a pool ball, bruv. Don't matter what colour. Alright it matters a bit. Not the black one, that's bad luck innit.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Peak. Absolute scenes. You are now an honorary Crow. Not really. But nearly.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: The Firm are rolling in Greggs vouchers. Bring us three and we'll call it a tax. A Crows tax. A Crowtax. I came up with that. Don't steal it.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Tax collected. HMRC could never. Here, have a screwdriver, it's surplus to requirements.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: {target} from the Firm keeps calling us 'the Pigeons'. We are not pigeons. Go and explain the difference. With feeling.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Did he say 'crow'? Tell me he said 'crow'. Legend.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: Get to the flagpole during yard and give us a proper chant. Loud. Tuneful is optional. Heartfelt is not.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: I heard that from the showers. I welled up. Here, you earned it.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: Five-a-side needs a goalpost. A canteen tray is basically a goalpost if you squint. Or if you're Gaz, who can't see anyway.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: Back of the net. Literally, now we've got a net. It's a tray. Shut up.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: {target} of the Northern Mob says the Lions bottled it in the last ruck. We did not bottle it. We tactically retreated. Go and correct him.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: Tactical retreat avenged. Have a sock. It's my lucky one. It's been through a lot.

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: The books don't balance. We're two socks short. Find them. I'll know if they're not clean. I won't check. But I'll know.

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: Ledger balanced. You may have a biscuit. Metaphorically. Here is a Greggs voucher.

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: {target} owes us three Twixes and an apology. We will take the apology out of his face. You will take it, I mean. I do accounts.

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: Debt settled. Interest accrued. You are a credit to the profession.

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: Canteen tea is a crime against Yorkshire. Healthcare keeps proper teabags in the cupboard. Liberate them. Do it for the North.

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: Now that is a brew. I could cry. I won't. But I could.

speaker: Big Stu (prisoner, cell D1)
line: Get us a toothbrush. Mine's gone manky. Don't ask what I used it for. Grout. I used it for grout.

speaker: Big Stu (prisoner, cell D1)
line: Minty fresh. You're alright, you.

speaker: Biscuits Reece (prisoner, cell C9)
line: Give this to {target} on {wing} wing. If anyone asks, it's from your nan. If he asks, it's from me. If he laughs, it's from you.

speaker: Lee (prisoner, cell A3)
line: Custard creams. A whole packet. I've had a day. I've had a week. I've had a fifteen-year stretch, frankly.

speaker: Lee (prisoner, cell A3)
line: Oh, that's the stuff. You're a gent. A crook, but a gent.

speaker: Mrs Battenberg (officer, C wing escort)
line: The governor confiscated my Racing Post and then lost it in the games room. Three horses circled. One's called Lord Biscuitwick. Find it, and I might not see you once.

speaker: Mrs Battenberg (officer, C wing escort)
line: Lord Biscuitwick, each way. Lovely. Right. Next time I see you somewhere funny, I didn't.

speaker: Ms Clutterbuck (officer, D wing landing)
line: Officers' biscuit tin is empty and it's only Tuesday. Custard creams. You didn't get them from me, I didn't ask, and this conversation is a figment.

speaker: Ms Clutterbuck (officer, D wing landing)
line: What biscuits? I see no biscuits. Mmf. Carry on, you.

speaker: Mrs Shufflebotham (officer, D wing central)
line: I've lost my reading glasses somewhere in the yard. Leopard print. On a little beaded chain. If you laugh, I'm nicking you.

speaker: Mrs Shufflebotham (officer, D wing central)
line: Oh, I can see! Here, I found this bent bit of wire in my bag. No idea how it got there. You have it.

speaker: Mr Crumpet (officer, A wing escort)
line: Somebody's brewing hooch on {wing} wing. Smells like a fruit bowl died in a sock. Have a sniff around {cell} and tell me what you find. Discreetly. Like a bloodhound in slippers.

speaker: Mr Crumpet (officer, A wing escort)
line: A bin bag of fermented oranges. Classic. Good work. Don't tell anyone it was you. They'll know anyway.

speaker: Mr Sidebottom (officer, C wing central)
line: I'm on a double and my feet are killing me. Keep your nose clean till {time}. No warnings, no nonsense, no 'accidents' with the mop.

speaker: Mr Sidebottom (officer, C wing central)
line: Not a peep. A miracle. Here, for your services to my bunions.

speaker: Mr Wellbeloved (officer, B wing central)
line: {target} has topped the officers' fantasy league three weeks running and he's not even IN it. Find out who he's picked as captain. For security reasons.

speaker: Mr Wellbeloved (officer, B wing central)
line: His NAN? Genius. Diabolical. Right, I owe you one. One.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: Alright? Keith. I do the X-ray. Twenty-two years. Seen it all: phones in pies, a ferret in a duvet, a whole set of drums in a mattress once. Don't ask.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: We never spoke. My eyes are terrible today. Terrible.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: Blue raspberry? And a sausage roll? ...You know, I get this cataract on Thursdays. Today feels like a Thursday. Eleven o'clock van. I'll be very busy with my sausage roll.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: Oh, that's the good blue. Right. If a basket comes through looking like a person, I'll assume it's a very lumpy duvet. Today only, mind.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: A blue drink. The proper blue, from the vending machine in visits. And a sausage roll from the canteen. One of each. I am a man of simple tastes.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Ah! The Greggs Bandit, in my chapel! I have prayed for you, and separately for the sausage rolls. Now, a small crisis: somebody has stolen three of my hymn books. Three! I have a choir of eleven and a man called Tiny who only knows the words to Jerusalem. Bring them back and I will owe you one. A proper one.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Three Greggs vouchers from the collection plate, which I shall confess on Sunday. And a favour. If you are ever somewhere you should not be, and an officer has you by the collar, I may well remember that you were at choir practice. Once. I can lie once. Twice is a habit.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Bless you. Word on the landing is one is levelling the pool table in the games room, one is a soap dish in the showers, and one is holding up the bench press in the gym. Hymns Ancient and Modern, red covers, moustaches on all the bishops. Do not ask about the moustaches.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Any luck? The games room, the showers and the gym. If anyone asks, you are doing the Lord's work. Technically you are.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Is that...? All three! And only slightly damp. You are a wonder.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Three vouchers, as promised. And remember: choir practice. If an officer ever drags you off somewhere awkward, you were with me, singing the alto line. Once, mind. I'm a chaplain, not a solicitor.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Choir practice is still on, if you ever need it. Once.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: The hymn books are back in the pews. Tiny is learning a second hymn. Miracles do happen.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: I've already lied for you once. I spent all of Sunday apologising. Panto auditions are Thursday, though.

speaker: Mr Ramsbottom (officer, D wing escort)
line: Right, {name}, you're coming with me.

speaker: Ms Doubleday (officer, B wing landing)
line: {name}! Behind your door!

speaker: Mr Gristle (officer, C wing landing)
line: What's all this then? {thing}. Confiscated.

speaker: Mr Featherstonehaugh (officer, D wing gate)
line: Clean. Off you go.

speaker: Ms Puddifoot (officer, C wing gate)
line: Where's {name} gone?!

speaker: Chalky Dwayne (prisoner, cell D2)
line: ON MY FLOOR?! ...{name}. It was YOU.

speaker: Dwayne (prisoner, cell B2)
line: WHO DID THIS?! ...{name}. It was YOU.

speaker: Spanner Craig (prisoner, cell A6)
line: WHO DID THIS?! ...Was it YOU, {someone}?!

speaker: Kettle Tariq (prisoner, cell A9)
line: WHO DID THIS?! I will find out. I WILL find out.

speaker: Spanner Kev (prisoner, cell A2)
line: And stay out.

speaker: Neil (prisoner, cell B6)
line: Oi. {name}. Out of my cell. NOW.

speaker: Biscuits Paddy (prisoner, cell D1)
line: Can I help you, young man? This is my cell.

speaker: Reece (prisoner, cell A9)
line: You're not meant to be in here. I'm just saying.

speaker: Sausage Gaz (prisoner, cell C1)
line: What you doing in my cell, {name}?

speaker: Jamal (prisoner, cell A3)
line: Oi. Out. This is my peter.

speaker: Chalky Neil (prisoner, cell D6)
line: You lost? This is my cell. Get out.

speaker: Scouse (prisoner, cell B4)
line: Some of us have to live here, you know. I shall be writing to my MP.

speaker: Wayne (prisoner, cell A2)
line: Right. I'm telling.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: You're getting cut.

speaker: Ryan (prisoner, cell A4)
line: Nobody walks into a firm cell.

speaker: Fingers Dave (prisoner, cell C0)
line: Right. You asked for it.

speaker: Mr Pickles (officer, B wing gate)
line: Well, well. Look what crawled out.

speaker: Mr Snodgrass (officer, B wing escort)
line: Oi! Get your hands off!

speaker: Mr Higginbottom (officer, A wing gate)
line: Not now, {name}. You're not on the movement list.

speaker: Mrs Thistlethwaite (officer, A wing central)
line: Assaulting an officer?!

speaker: Mr Featherstonehaugh (officer, D wing gate)
line: *yawns* I'll just... rest my eyes... for a...

speaker: Big Scouse (prisoner, cell D4)
line: Who's had my trousers?! And my KEYS?!

speaker: Mr Ramsbottom (officer, D wing escort)
line: I'm not eating anything you've touched, Bandit. I've read the memo.

speaker: Ms Bottomley (officer, A wing landing)
line: Ooh, go on then. Don't tell the Governor.

speaker: Ms Doubleday (officer, B wing landing)
line: Is that a Greggs? For me? You shouldn't have. Mmf.

speaker: Mrs Thistlethwaite (officer, A wing central)
line: Well, it would be rude not to.

speaker: Mr Snodgrass (officer, B wing escort)
line: Lovely. Right, I have rounds to do.

speaker: Mr Featherstonehaugh (officer, D wing gate)
line: Who put that up there?

speaker: Ms Bottomley (officer, A wing landing)
line: I've got my eye on you. Both of them. This one's glass.

speaker: Mr Crumpet (officer, A wing escort)
line: Don't even think about it. I can see you thinking. Your lips move.

speaker: Mr Pickles (officer, B wing gate)
line: Move along before I find a reason.

speaker: Mrs Battenberg (officer, C wing escort)
line: Ah. You. Just the person. Keep your voice down.

speaker: Mr Higginbottom (officer, A wing gate)
line: Psst. Over here. No, act natural. NATURAL.

speaker: Mrs Shufflebotham (officer, D wing central)
line: You look like someone who can keep their mouth shut. Can you? Good.

speaker: Mr Gristle (officer, C wing landing)
line: Ah, the Greggs Bandit. I've got my eye on you. And on my lunch.

speaker: Mr Sidebottom (officer, C wing central)
line: What do you want? If it is the telly remote, the answer is no.

speaker: Mr Snodgrass (officer, B wing escort)
line: Keep your nose clean and we will get along famously.

speaker: Ms Bottomley (officer, A wing landing)
line: Not now, I'm on my break. I'm always on my break.

speaker: Ms Puddifoot (officer, C wing gate)
line: Lovely weather for it. Not that you would know.

speaker: Ms Doubleday (officer, B wing landing)
line: If you're after the toilet roll, there is none. There's never any.

speaker: Toast Marcus (prisoner, cell C7)
line: Cheers.

speaker: Two-Sugars Ryan (prisoner, cell C5)
line: After what you have done to my lads? Not for all the sausage rolls in Grim-on-the-Moor.

speaker: Spanner Lee (prisoner, cell C3)
line: Pleasure doing business. Give the word (G) on {wing} wing and my lads go up. You have two days.

speaker: Tommo (prisoner, cell A1)
line: {thing} Nobody kicks off without the firm that runs the landing. Pay the boss, and mind who you pay: the Firm and the Crows hate each other, and so do the Lions and the Mob.

speaker: Spanner Marcus (prisoner, your cellmate)
line: Word is {thing}{thing} All since your little stunt.

speaker: Pie Ash (prisoner, cell D8)
line: Every time you mess about, the screws come down on all of us. Keep it up.

speaker: Chalky Taff (prisoner, cell B3)
line: Mind your own.

speaker: Liam (prisoner, cell A6)
line: The screws carry the keys on their belts. Get behind one while he's arguing about the footy.

speaker: Spanner Callum (prisoner, cell A4)
line: Toothpaste in the strike plate sets like concrete. Door looks locked. It isn't. Whitening AND escaping.

speaker: Big Darren (prisoner, cell C5)
line: Bang on your door at night like you are dying and they have to take you to healthcare. Make it a good groan. They score you.

speaker: Dom (prisoner, cell B9)
line: Proper kick-off on the landing and every screw in the place comes running. Doors get left open. Kettles get left on.

speaker: Mo (prisoner, cell B0)
line: Phones are taped. Never say when. Never say how. Talk about your nan. Everybody talks about their nan.

speaker: Toast Shane (prisoner, cell C8)
line: Lads used to run a red rag up the yard flagpole for their people on the road. Like semaphore, but dodgier.

speaker: Dodgy Kieran (prisoner, cell C8)
line: Maintenance has every tool you could want. Shame it's behind a red door. Shame about a lot of things.

speaker: Mad Jock (prisoner, cell D4)
line: The vents run over everything except the cells. Except some cells... I have said too much. I always say too much.

speaker: Jase (prisoner, cell B9)
line: Two sheets knotted make a rope. Bend a fork and tape it on and it is a hook. Blue Peter taught me that. Sort of.

speaker: Kieran (prisoner, cell A8)
line: Soap takes a key impression lovely. Melt a fork into it with a lighter. Do not do it in the canteen. Ask me how I know.

speaker: Gravy Tommo (prisoner, cell C1)
line: Chew soap before you fake it. Froth sells it. Tastes like a disappointing Tuesday.

speaker: Biscuits Kev (prisoner, cell C3)
line: Officers get bored. Bored officers want favours. Do one and they might not see you. Once.

speaker: Chalky Rich (prisoner, cell C0)
line: Never trust a man who says 'with all due respect'. Or a man in maroon. Or the fish pie.

speaker: Toast Ash (prisoner, cell B8)
line: See that grille behind the table? Maintenance never put it on the list. Screws are rusted to nothing; a spoon'd turn them. Goes up into the ducts. Don't get caught in there, mind, or they'll weld it.

speaker: Two-Sugars Callum (prisoner, cell C4)
line: They've been at all the locks since you started. Keep your head down for a day or two. They forget faster than you think. They don't, actually.

speaker: Big Ollie (prisoner, cell B2)
line: What do YOU want?

speaker: Stu (prisoner, cell B1)
line: Oh, it is you. Marvellous. Smashing. Go away.

speaker: Pie Liam (prisoner, cell C6)
line: You know who I am. {someone} run {wing} wing.

speaker: Terry (prisoner, cell B7)
line: You lost?

speaker: Chalky Fergus (prisoner, cell B5)
line: You look like you want something. Everyone wants something.

speaker: Vince (prisoner, cell B7)
line: Looking for something? I can get things. Not Freddos. Never ask me for Freddos.

speaker: Big Barry (prisoner, cell D6)
line: Psst. Batteries, wire, a lighter, a screwdriver. Cash or Greggs vouchers. Mostly vouchers. Only vouchers.

speaker: Kettle Wayne (prisoner, cell C2)
line: Alright, {name}.

speaker: Gravy Jamal (prisoner, cell C4)
line: Oi oi, it's the Greggs Bandit!

speaker: Kettle Ade (prisoner, cell D3)
line: Is it true you nicked a festive bake? In OCTOBER? Respect.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: My cousin works in that Greggs. She has nightmares.

speaker: Paddy (prisoner, cell B1)
line: Alright?

speaker: Biscuits Jase (prisoner, cell D9)
line: Y'alright, our kid?

speaker: Big Scouse (prisoner, cell D4)
line: Wotcha.

speaker: Pie Jonno (prisoner, cell D0)
line: Ey up.

speaker: Wonky Terry (prisoner, cell D7)
line: Alright, chief? Kettle on?

speaker: Kettle Rocco (prisoner, cell D8)
line: Do I know you? I feel like I know you. Did you do my mum's guttering?

speaker: Posh Fergus (prisoner, cell D5)
line: Evening, officer... hang on.

speaker: Barry (prisoner, cell B6)
line: Since when do they let screws wear trainers?

speaker: Jonno (prisoner, cell B0)
line: Is that you? It is, isn't it. Say nothing. Say NOTHING.

speaker: Chalky Ade (prisoner, cell B3)
line: Nice frock.

speaker: Little Dom (prisoner, cell D9)
line: Alright, darling? ...Oh no.

speaker: Sausage Ollie (prisoner, cell D2)
line: Is that the panto wig? Bold.

speaker: Biscuits Craig (prisoner, cell C7)
line: You've got lovely ankles, I'll give you that.

speaker: Mrs Thistlethwaite (officer, A wing central)
line: Right. New uniform. Nobody mention the boxers.

speaker: Mr Wellbeloved (officer, B wing central)
line: Hang about. {officer} is six foot four with a moustache. You are neither.

speaker: Ms Clutterbuck (officer, D wing landing)
line: Warrant card? ...That's a Tesco Clubcard.

speaker: Mr Ramsbottom (officer, D wing escort)
line: Madam, you have a prison number on your neck. And a beard.

speaker: Mrs Shufflebotham (officer, D wing central)
line: Lovely to see you, Mrs... Mrs... that's a pillowcase, not a handbag.

speaker: Mr Wellbeloved (officer, B wing central)
line: This pillowcase is breathing.

speaker: Mr Crumpet (officer, A wing escort)
line: Since when do towels wear trainers?

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Lovely to see a new face. Well. An old face. A face.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Panto auditions Thursday. We need a back half of a horse.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: The Lord moves in mysterious ways. So does the tea trolley.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Choir at four. Bring your lungs.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: The Governor? Green Jag, private plate: R P {thing}. Polishes it in the staff car park every lunchtime. Says it's the only thing in here that doesn't answer back.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: A blue drink. The proper blue, from the vending machine in visits. And a sausage roll from the canteen. {thing} of each, mind. Inflation.

speaker: Mr Higginbottom (officer, A wing gate)
line: What was that? ...In the vents?

speaker: Ms Doubleday (officer, B wing landing)
line: Who threw that?

speaker: Mr Snodgrass (officer, B wing escort)
line: Hello?

speaker: Carl (prisoner, cell B5)
line: From WHO? ...Tell him yes. No. Tell him maybe. Tell him I'm thinking about it.

speaker: Bins Tariq (prisoner, cell C9)
line: Is this lipstick? Is this... is this Rimmel? Oh, he shouldn't have.

speaker: Dodgy Vince (prisoner, cell D7)
line: Right. I'm going to read this in private and you are going to forget my face.

speaker: Big Stu (prisoner, cell D1)
line: Well? Chop chop. {thing}

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: I'm not getting any younger. Neither are you, in here. {thing}

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: Tick tock. I said tick tock. {thing}

speaker: Biscuits Reece (prisoner, cell C9)
line: Actually, forget it. Wrong time, wrong face.

speaker: Lee (prisoner, cell A3)
line: Your loss. Literally.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)
line: Suit yourself, sunshine.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Fine. I will remember this. I remember everything.

speaker: Bins Nathan (prisoner, cell C6)
line: It's coming home!

speaker: Kettle Carl (prisoner, cell D5)
line: Oi oi!

speaker: Bins Darren (prisoner, cell A5)
line: Get in!

line: Shut UP!

speaker: Little Taff (prisoner, cell D3)
line: Grass.

line: Out. Out! Weirdo.

speaker: Mr Featherstonehaugh (officer, D wing gate)

speaker: Mr Ramsbottom (officer, D wing escort)

speaker: Mrs Battenberg (officer, C wing escort)

speaker: Ms Bottomley (officer, A wing landing)

speaker: Mr Pickles (officer, B wing gate)

speaker: Ms Clutterbuck (officer, D wing landing)
line: *studies ceiling intently*

speaker: Mr Wellbeloved (officer, B wing central)

speaker: Mr Featherstonehaugh (officer, D wing gate)

speaker: Mrs Shufflebotham (officer, D wing central)

line: Is that... Colgate? In MY lock?

speaker: Mr Gristle (officer, C wing landing)
line: Minty. Very minty. Very NICKED.

speaker: Mr Pickles (officer, B wing gate)
line: Behind your doors, gents!

speaker: Mrs Thistlethwaite (officer, A wing central)
line: Bang-up! Come on, I've got Corrie on at nine!

speaker: Mr Ramsbottom (officer, D wing escort)
line: Doors in five minutes!

speaker: Ms Clutterbuck (officer, D wing landing)
line: Chop chop! Teeth, wee, bed!

speaker: Ms Puddifoot (officer, C wing gate)
line: Right, what's all this then? If it's another spider, I'm off.

speaker: Mr Higginbottom (officer, A wing gate)
line: A rat, you say? Where? I hate rats. Where is it?

speaker: Mr Pickles (officer, B wing gate)
line: This had better be good. I left a brew for this.

speaker: Mr Crumpet (officer, A wing escort)
line: Waste of my time. Again.

speaker: Ms Doubleday (officer, B wing landing)
line: There is no rat. There was never a rat.

speaker: Mr Featherstonehaugh (officer, D wing gate)
line: I'm putting this in my notebook. In capitals.

speaker: Ms Bottomley (officer, A wing landing)
line: You look fine to me. Have a glass of water and a word with yourself.

speaker: Ms Puddifoot (officer, C wing gate)
line: That's not a groan, that's an amateur groan. Get some kip.

speaker: Mr Higginbottom (officer, A wing gate)
line: Dying, are we? Again? Shame. Night night.

speaker: Mr Crumpet (officer, A wing escort)
line: Alright {name}, out you come. Slowly. If you're sick on my shoes there'll be trouble.

speaker: Ms Clutterbuck (officer, D wing landing)
line: Suit yourself.

speaker: Mrs Battenberg (officer, C wing escort)
line: Keep up.

speaker: Mr Sidebottom (officer, C wing central)
line: Sit on the bed. Nurse'll be along. She's on her biscuit break, so, a while.

speaker: Mr Gristle (officer, C wing landing)
line: Right. Nurse says two paracetamol and stop being a drama queen. Back to bed.

speaker: Wonky Shane (prisoner, cell A8)
line: Screws out!

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)
line: Oi oi oi!

speaker: Dodgy Rocco (prisoner, cell B8)
line: We want proper gravy!

speaker: Jock (prisoner, cell B4)
line: Free the telly!

speaker: Two-Sugars Mo (prisoner, cell D0)
line: Bring back the custard!

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Come on then!

speaker: Nathan (prisoner, cell A5)
line: Have it!

speaker: Gaz (prisoner, cell A0)
line: You what?!

speaker: Bins Nathan (prisoner, cell C6)
line: That's for the custard!

speaker: Biscuits Jase (prisoner, cell D9)
line: Not the face!

speaker: Two-Sugars Mo (prisoner, cell D0)
line: {someone} send their regards.

speaker: Spanner Marcus (prisoner, your cellmate)
line: Wrong place, {name}.

speaker: Big Ollie (prisoner, cell B2)
line: Nowhere to run in here.

speaker: Ryan (prisoner, cell A4)
line: Guv... {name}'s carrying. You didn't hear it from me. I'm not here.
